description: Standup reads your git commits and your agents' sessions and writes the end-of-day update you can no longer write from memory.

ui.aboutDescription: What {site} reads, what it writes and who made it.
ui.notFoundBody: This page does not exist. The rest of the site is still here.
ui.aboutBody: {site} is a Claude Code plugin with two skills, eod-review for a day and eow-review for a week. Radu Ceuca built it to answer one question at the end of the day: what did I do.
ui.headline: You and your agents were busy all day. Doing what?
ui.ledeMorning: It’s {time}, the team standup is coming and yesterday is a blur. Three agents kept going after you closed the laptop. What did they finish? What did you? Standup goes through yesterday’s work, yours and your agents’, and hands you the update before the coffee is done.
ui.ledeMidmorning: It’s {time}, you opened four Claude Code sessions before your first meeting and you already cannot say which one is doing what. It is not even lunch. Standup goes through your work and your agents’ work so far and tells you where the day stands.
ui.ledeAfternoon: It’s {time}, half the day is gone and it went somewhere. A branch you do not remember creating has six commits on it. Somebody wants a status by end of day. Standup goes through your work and your agents’ work and writes down what has shipped so far.
ui.ledeEvening: It’s {time}, you have a dozen Claude Code sessions mid-flight, a handful of branches and no clear memory of the morning. How did we get here? Did we get anything done today? Manager asking for update. Client asking for status? You need to pick up your kid from acting classes in 1h. Standup goes through your work and your agents’ work and writes the summary for you.
ui.ledeNight: It’s {time}, you should be asleep and two agents are still going. By morning you will not remember what you asked them for. Standup goes through the night’s work when you wake up and tells you what they did while you slept.
ui.installNote: Not published yet. This command works once the repository is public. It reads files on your own disk and uploads nothing.
ui.readsTitle: You get four to six lines you can say out loud.
ui.readsBody: Commits from every branch of every repo you point it at, grouped into things a person would recognise. Paste it into Slack, or keep it as a catch-up with your own day.
ui.weekTitle: On Friday, ask for the week.
ui.weekBody: eow-review covers Monday to Sunday, day by day. Monday's work is still there on Friday, which is more than most of us can say.
ui.numbersTitle: It also says what the agents cost.
ui.numbersBody: Tokens are counted per folder, branch and day, dead ends included. The dollar figure is an estimate at API list prices, and the report labels it that way. On a subscription you pay none of it per token.
ui.requirements: Needs Python 3.9 or later and git. Runs on macOS and Linux.
ui.askTitle: "What did you work on today?" is a hard question now.
ui.askBody: You started three things before lunch. An agent finished two of them, and another ran in a worktree you forgot about. The work happened. Your memory of it did not.
ui.agentsTitle: It reads Claude Code, Codex, Grok, Gemini CLI, opencode and Cowork.
ui.agentsBody: What shipped comes from git, so it covers the work whoever wrote it, you or any agent. Tokens and cost come from those six, including sessions Superconductor or Conductor ran in a separate worktree. Cursor and Antigravity keep no token counts on disk, so the report counts their sessions.
ui.projectsTitle: Work, consulting and side projects stay apart.
ui.projectsBody: Point it at the folder that holds all your repos and one report covers every project. Name your groups, say work, consulting and personal, and each gets its own section with its own commits and cost. The update you send to one never mentions another.
ui.installOther: Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and opencode run the same two skills from your skills folder.
